method: Written from the model's training knowledge of the area. No live lookup, no aerial imagery, no OSM query, no site visit.

confidence.area_character: medium — KT23 is a well-known Surrey commuter village and its general building stock is the kind of thing a language model does hold
confidence.proportions: low to medium — the weights below are a considered estimate, not a survey. The first draft made every roof clay terracotta; interwar and post-war Surrey is mostly brown and grey concrete tile, which is the sort of thing this file exists to be corrected on.
confidence.street_level: low — nothing here is specific to the HP sector, and should not be read as such
confidence.landmarks: medium-high for the named ones; they are notable enough to be recalled rather than inferred

character: Great and Little Bookham: a Surrey commuter village between Leatherhead and Effingham, on the Mole Valley line. Predominantly interwar and post-war low-density suburban housing — detached and semi-detached, two storeys, generous plots with mature trees, laid out on cul-de-sacs and crescents off a few through-roads. A short older core around the church with some genuinely old fabric. Red and brown brick dominates, with render, pebbledash and tile-hanging common on 1930s stock. Roofs are overwhelmingly pitched, plain concrete or clay tile, a good share hipped rather than gabled. Very little that is tall: almost nothing above three storeys. Bookham Common to the north-west and Polesden Lacey's estate to the south are both National Trust, and the surrounding land is farmland, woodland and paddock rather than open moor.

known_gaps: No coordinates are given for anything. This profile cannot place a building; it can only say what a building already known to exist is probably like.
The HP sector is not distinguished from the rest of KT23. Treat every number here as 'typical of Bookham', not 'true of this street'.
Proportions are a judgement, not a count. The honest test is whether they beat the sim's existing UK-wide defaults, not whether they are right.
Building type is chosen from footprint size alone, because that is the only evidence OSM gives. A 200 m2 footprint that is really a village hall will be dressed as a house.
